tag: Episode 52 · A Promise by the Cherry-Blossom River
title: A Promise by the Cherry-Blossom River

beats.t: The reply came at dawn three days later. Seeing the 1 gone, Yeoni nearly rolled off her bed.
[ Text · Park Byeongha: Screen broke. Only just saw this. Thursday, four. East bench. Won't be late. ]
Thursday. As soon as class ended, Yeoni took her bicycle to the river. The bench she and Byeongha had chosen was marked on her phone’s map. Thirty minutes until their meeting.
She took a wrong turn at the first bridge, then wheeled back down toward the river. She wasn’t late, but kept checking the time.
Thirty minutes is plenty. Why has the clock jumped ahead every time I look?
[ App · Kang Saebyeok: Checked the bench location? Your appointment won’t fall with the petals, so take your time. Consultation fee later. ]
Thanks for passing on his number, but why a consultation fee? Do I get a refund for the wrong turn?
Even so, Yeoni pedaled. Today they'd deliberately worn mismatched socks. Yellow on the left, stripes on the right.
He’ll notice the socks first again. Once I hear him nag, maybe I’ll be able to talk like usual too.
Choosing her socks that morning, Yeoni had rehearsed her greeting over and over. She never quite managed to say “I missed you” aloud. She hoped the mismatched socks might say it for her.
[ App · Moka: Meeting him today, right? If you run out of words, play my rap. No guarantees about the mood. ]
That's interference, not encouragement.
The river wind carried petals away. Yeoni slowed her pedaling. More than losing her way, she worried she would cry the moment she saw his face.
If the flowers fall, we can come again. And whatever I can’t say today, I can say next time.
Yeoni gripped the handlebars. The center of their palm felt slightly warm. Where the Metal fragment had stayed.
She reached the chosen bench just before four. As she parked her bicycle, her grip slipped. It toppled toward the grass, and she busied herself rummaging in her bag.
I found the right place. Why am I the one malfunctioning?
At the top of her notebook: four o’clock, riverside bench. Beneath it, she had added a small “Neo” beside Park Byeongha. The familiar name steadied her breathing.
I can just start with his name. Like I always did.
As they closed the notebook, a petal settled between the pages. Yeoni left it there instead of brushing it away.
Then a sneeze came from the far end of the bench. Yeoni turned.
A white umbrella leaned against the bench. Beside it sat a man with a book open on his knees. A stray cat crouched at his feet.
Ah, sorry. I'm allergic to cats.
Then why not shoo it away?
It sat here first. This is its spot.
The man's hair was silver. Beneath the river-tousled strands were those blunt eyes. He only nodded as though seeing her for the first time.
Yeoni held her breath. The person whose hand she'd first held on the boat. And now he was pretending not to know her.
Your bicycle fell over.
Oh. Yes. I know. Deliberately.
Never met someone who knocks it over deliberately.
The man looked back at his book, then stopped. His gaze caught at Yeoni's ankles, between the yellow sock and the striped one.
Excuse me. Your socks don't match.
Three seconds. That was how long the stranger act lasted. Yeoni bit her lip; he closed his book with an oops expression.
…Tried pretending I didn't know you. Socks ruined it.
Couldn't last three seconds. One star for acting.
I saw your palm on the bus window. Ran, but couldn't catch it.
Then you could've waved. I got off at the next stop and ran back!
Byeongha pressed his lips together, looking as though he might cry if he tried to smile. Seeing his face, Yeoni broke into a smile too.
That's why I came early today. An hour.
An hour? Did you practice that act for an hour too?
Ten minutes was quite sufficient for rehearsal. The rest was spent waiting for a cat to vacate the seat.
Stop being polite. You're giving me chills.
A shame. All right.
Byeongha rubbed his temple, looking embarrassed. The familiar gesture finally let Yeoni relax her shoulders.
Byeongha righted the bicycle and handed it to Yeoni. She left one side of the handlebars to him. They walked toward the river at the same pace. There was no need to hurry after each other anymore.
The cherry-tree path stretched along the river. Petals blew onto their shoulders. The last petals.
Asked three cats for directions this week. All they did was make me sneeze.
Why ask cats?
Thought they'd understand. Habits are frightening.
So that's why your sleeve had white fur. Saebyeok told me.
That fortune-teller checks people's sleeves too?
He reads palms. Anything near a hand is fair game.
Brushed my sleeves today. Check.
Checked. One hair left. White.
Only then did Byeongha laugh aloud. Yeoni couldn't stop laughing either. A petal caught in his silver hair.
Want to introduce ourselves again? No hidden names.
Park Byeongha. And you are?
Park Byeongha. Yeoni rolled the name silently in their mind. The name first read at the Lovers card. The name that would make him disappear.
Calling it could no longer make him disappear. Her card had restored names and memories to their owners. She wanted to hear that truth aloud here in reality too.
Still. There’s the name I gave you too.
She shook her head. There was another name to call. The one she'd used in the Void, clutching one note, to call back someone she'd forgotten entirely.
I'm Yeoni. And may I ask a favor?
What is it?
From now on, I'll use the name I gave you. Please answer right away.
Neo.
The wind stopped. Falling petals seemed to pause briefly in midair. Park Byeongha stopped walking.
Ah.
He looked at his hand. His name had been called, yet his fingertips weren't transparent. He opened and closed his hand twice, checking.
The first raindrop fell. One ring, then another spread across the river.
She opened the yellow umbrella from her bag, handle wrapped in three layers of tape, and tilted half toward him. Her left shoulder began to soak.
Yeoni.
Yes. It's me. Mismatched socks.
Your shoulder's getting wet. Give it here.
The playful formality fell away. Blunt, a little cheeky, and strangely tender at the edges. It was the voice she had wanted to hear all along.
No. I'm holding it today.
Still stubborn.
Byeongha wrapped his hand around hers on the shaft. The umbrella returned to the middle. This time, no part of him faded.
…Didn't lose you.
My hands aren't transparent. Even if I hold you like this… it's all right, isn't it?
My head. Just my head. You know how to pat it.
And Yeoni. Why are your socks mismatched again?
A test. You passed.
The stray cat following at their feet meowed. Park Byeongha sneezed. Yeoni laughed aloud.
The allergy survived. Couldn't they have fixed that when I returned? I'll have to call customer support myself.
Let's file a complaint. Only one person in the queue. Should connect quickly.
Your memories stayed with you after you came back, right? Your days as Byeongha and your days as Neo, both?
Both. Byeongha, going to work and paying rent. Neo, beside you. Even the hand you took on the boat.
Strangely, none of it gets mixed up. Maybe because both are me.
Then what should I call you? Byeongha? Neo?
Use the name you gave me. Neo. At work, Byeongha, please. Otherwise there's too much to explain.
I wasn't planning to visit your office. Now I am.
Byeongha laughed. A slightly awkward smile with one corner rising first. Yeoni felt they would never forget it now.
The sun tilted over the river. Petals drifted slowly on the water. They stood side by side against the riverside railing.
In the first spring, we promised to walk this road together. Never did.
What were we planning that spring? Not to fight, surely?
Nothing. Just a walk. Fighting could wait until afterward.
Then promise. Every spring, we walk here. Before the blossoms fall. Doing nothing.
Promises are for keeping. We take turns with the umbrella.
[ App notification · Seo Hanbi: Sea trip, second Saturday in May. One more person is welcome. No one who sheds fur. ]
Haven't shed fur in ages. Still bringing that up?
You still sneeze.
Yeoni replied: Adding one. Human. No fur. Sock inspector.
The sea will be a first. We never made it there that spring.
Then you roll the gimbap. One star if the sides split.
[ App notification · Kang Saebyeok: You found him. My daily forecast was right, so the fee is due. Also, his birth time, please. ]
Why is he still asking birth times?
He wants to read our compatibility. Yours and mine.
The Eul–Gyeong union is enough for us. We came all this way together.
Still curious, though. What score we'd get.
If it's not a hundred, don't see that fortune-teller again.
Smiling, Yeoni pocketed the phone and took Park Byeongha's hand. A human hand was larger than expected, and a little colder.
Your hand's cold. Because you're Gyeong Metal?
Your hand's warm. Because you're Eul Wood.
Hand in hand, they walked along the river. The stray cat followed at a distance. Park Byeongha sneezed again. The last petal drifted downriver.
